newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambia evacuates diplomats' families from Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Zambia evacuates diplomats' families from Zaire.

text.p: The Zambian government has evacuated families of diplomatic staff from neighbouring Zaire because of the civil war there, a foreign affairs official said on Tuesday.
Key diplomatic staff would stay in the Zairean capital, Kinshasa and the country's second city, Lubumbashi, for the time being, said the official, who declined to be identified.
"The families of diplomatic staff in Lubumbashi were evacuated to Chililabombwe, while the families of Kinshasa-based staff were flown to Lusaka."

He was unable to say how many people had been evacuated, but said Zambia had about 20 diplomatic staff in Zaire. About a quarter of the country is now under the control of rebels led by Laurent Kabila.
The only people crossing into Zambia from Lubumbashi, about 50 km (32 miles) from the border, are traders who say they do not fear their city will fall to rebels any time soon.
One trader said he believed the rebels would only get there in a couple of months, but there would be no fighting.
"There will be no trouble in Lubumbashi," he said.
Guards at Zambia's Kasumbalesa border post on the main road between Lubumbashi and Chililabombwe, a copper mining town, said they had not recorded any Zairean refugees crossing the border.
The only people who had come across the border because of fears of violence were foreigners who had been in Lubumbashi.
A group of 60 Asian women and children had crossed the border at the weekend, one immigration official said.
Many had said they would stay with relatives or friends in Lusaka until the situation in Lubumbashi became clearer. The men had apparently stayed to protect their businesses.
Zaireans crossing into Zambia buy maize meal and other essentials, which they then ferry back home in wheelbarrows.
Relief groups said the border region was quiet, and the Red Cross of Zambia was considering withdrawing officials.

"We sent people to the border in anticipation of an influx, but there have been no Zaireans fleeing from Lubumbashi so far. We are thinking of recalling our people until their presence is required," a Red Cross official said.
Last month about 3,000 Zaireans fleeing fighting in Zaire's northeast crossed into Zambia by boat on Lake Tanganyika, seeking safe passage to other parts of their homeland.
